source_context_translations.translation: Nameless, it is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; having a name, it is the mother of the myriad things.
Therefore, constantly without desires, one can observe its subtlety,
constantly having desires, one can observe its outward manifestation;
these two arise together yet are named differently; together they are called the mysterious.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to exist or be present, introducing the existence of something
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Existential, often framing the presence of something in a scene or statement.
Sentence Translations (English): When there is the Way, there is order; when there is no Way, there is disorder.
In so vast a world, misfortune and blessing surely exist.
There was no one in the room, yet the lamp still gave light.
In the heart of a good person, there is often fear.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to hold or be equipped with something, or to be characterized by something as one’s possession
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Possessive or attributive, focusing on ownership, presence in one’s domain, or being endowed with a quality.
Sentence Translations (English): When a state has treasures, the people value themselves.
A gentleman has a sense of shame; a petty man does not.
My household has a thousand volumes of books.
His words are trustworthy, so people esteem him.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to have a name, that is, to be designated or identified by a name rather than remaining nameless
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In attributive use, marking possession or the state of being named, not existential existence.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): introduces the means, method, or instrument used to carry out an action
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Instrumental or means-marking, often preceding the tool, method, or basis of action.
Sentence Translations (English): Rule the state by the Way, and the people will be at peace.
The sage wins people over by virtue.
A boat moves by wind; a cart moves by horse.
I know from this that it is so.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): marks a logical result or inference, introducing a conclusion drawn from what precedes
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Inferential or connective, linking a previous statement to a resulting action or judgment.
Sentence Translations (English): The Way is ever nonaction; hence the world transforms of itself.
The many people are confused; hence they do not know the root.
Water benefits the myriad things; hence it dwells below.
Therefore, when desires are removed and few, one can preserve one’s true nature.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): introduces the purpose or intended result of the following action
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Purposive, not instrumental; it marks the goal rather than the means.
contextual_sense.Translation (English): in order to; so as to

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to go after, request, or strive to obtain something
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A common alternative reading in which the term denotes active seeking rather than a boundary.
Sentence Translations (English): A gentleman does not seek fame.
He does not seek profit, so his heart is at ease.
The greedy often seek things outside themselves.
The sage does not use force to demand the world.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the visible edge, boundary, or outermost appearance of something
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Emphasizes the exterior or limit as opposed to the hidden interior or subtle source.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): used after a noun or pronoun to form a substantive meaning a person or thing characterized by the preceding expression
additional_senses.Nuance (English): General nominalizer, often yielding an entity, type, or role defined by what precedes it.
Sentence Translations (English): Those who know do not speak.
The benevolent love others.
Those who are good act as teachers.
The brave are without fear.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): a nominalized phrase referring back to the two items just mentioned
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Forms a noun-like reference to preceding particulars rather than adding lexical content.
